text: Thank you, Mr. Chair. Good evening, council. I'm bringing forward a report and a recommendation on a zoning amendment application for property at the corner of Rosedale and Rosedale and Roger Stevens. It's the former Monty school. The school has been vacant for a number of years, probably one of the most high profile visible development sites in the township. And we're certainly glad to see that there's been some interest in it. But in April, council held a public meeting to hear a proposal to accommodate essentially a light industrial high-tech business to be located within the school buildings. So it's according to our zoning bylaw, it best meets the classification of an industrial development and based on the existing definitions within our zoning bylaw, an industrial facility encapsulates the use and that's what they were applying for through the site specific zoning application. So we held the public meeting on the 20th. There was no public participation from plotting property owners, at least as far as anyone who provided us anything in writing or speaking at the meeting. The, what we had to work on, what staff and the developer's agent worked on since the public meeting was working with the zoning policy as a whole. So an industrial facility fits the parameters of what the proponents are looking to do here, but an industrial facility is a very broad definition in our zoning bylaw and it allows a whole range of uses, including some that are very, well, arguably quite incompatible at the location in terms of emissions and other sorts of industrial impact. So staff and the developer's agent were both working together to find a more scoped and specific definition to accommodate a very low impact industrial type use that would be a better fit at this location. And it's important as well, because if for whatever reason the business changes hands or evolves in the future, we want to make sure that the neighbors, the residences who live close by have some certainty that whatever goes in in the future, in the distant future is also compatible in their neighborhood. So that's the spirit of which we worked on some policy. And that's ultimately, it's a very prescriptive policy that's at the top of the recommendation, but it is something that's agreed to by, agreed to by the proponent and staff feel covers the proposed use, but also provides a little bit of certainty for the neighbors. So the staff report, of course, evaluates this application within the context of the official plan. And we did look at the provisions regarding new industrial development in the rural designation. So I think the site is generally well suited in terms of access. It's probably one of the most high traffic spots in the township, but has good access existing, an existing circular driveway. There's been no concerns raised from either the county or township public works departments or the health unit in terms of the servicing capabilities, no concerns raised by the Reno Valley Conservation Authority with respect to any natural hazard, natural heritage features that we had to look at. And ultimately it's a site that's already exist, it's already developed for traffic based on its former use. So if a council approves the zoning, a site plan application would of course deal with some of the more prescriptive design elements of the proposal. Ultimately, as far as we need to look at the land use compatibility as well. And that's why we had to take a closer look at the MOE's D6 guidelines. We looked at that through a zoning application on virtual earlier this year, and that's certainly applicable here, looking at sort of scoping the proposal to clarify that it is going to be a very low impact use. And I think that provision tying in the D6 guidelines into the zoning provision is very important in this case. So based on the feedback we received, or I guess from agencies as well as from the community that didn't raise any objections, we feel that this site is suited for an adaptive reuse that brings in some low impact employment uses to the community. I think the planning rationale highlighted one part of the one aspect of the OP that supported sort of value added or IT type industries as something that would, I guess, be a new concept within a township and ultimately provide an employment base and commercial or industrial taxation within the municipality. And of course, working with them to fit that within the zoning framework. So the recommendation of staff is that we approve or that council approves the application as or approves the zoning application as presented in the top of the report and a reasonable property to the industrial special, the light industrial special extension zone.
